/// If `SYMPOSIUM_HOOK_TRACE` is set to a file path, append a JSONL entry.
/// Used for integration testing to check what hooks occur when we invoke the agent.
fn write_hook_trace(agent: HookAgent, event: HookEvent, input: &str, response: &HookResponse) {
Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to open hook trace file"),

rationale:
**Implementation.** `run` calls `write_hook_trace` once after each successful `execute_hook` (a failed `execute_hook` or an unreadable stdin writes nothing, matching "answered event"). When `SYMPOSIUM_HOOK_TRACE` is set it appends one JSON line `{event, agent, input, output, exit_code, stderr}`; open/write failures only log (`best_effort`).

**Why false.** `output` is `serde_json::from_slice(&response.stdout).unwrap_or(Null)`, so any non-JSON stdout is recorded as `null` rather than recorded. Kiro's responses are plain text (its `serialize_output` in `src/hook_schema/kiro.rs` emits the context string), so every Kiro event with context has its output recorded as `null`. The same happens to an unparsable input. Either narrow the text ("the output parsed as JSON, or null") or record raw text. Untested in normal runs: the trace is only read by the real-agent harness (`tests/agent_harness/run_scenario.py`, `tests/hook_agent.rs` agent mode); `cargo test -q --test hook_agent` (simulation) passed 4 without exercising it.
requirement: When `SYMPOSIUM_HOOK_TRACE` names a file, `cargo agents hook` MUST append one JSON line per answered event recording the agent, the event, the input, the output when it is JSON (otherwise `null`), the exit code and stderr.
